page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with Hebrew and Greek words inline and an italic passage. No marginal notes on this printed page. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Below the text: signature "Aa 2" and catchword "Sacer-".

main_text.p: locus fuit, partim sacer, cujus ostio ad עזרה[?] atrium tendebant; partim profanus ac communis, cujus ostium ad oppositum conclavis latus. Hæc enim ostia locum vel sacrum vel profanum reddebant, quamvis uterque esset conjunctissimus. Unde Maimonid. tomo tertio י cum de templo agit, [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters] , Conclavia exstructa in loco sancto, & aperta versus profanum locum, si eorum tecta æqualia sint sive ἰσόπεδα[?] atrii pavimento; interius ipsorum, profanum; tecta vero sancta censentur: sin æqualia non fuerint; tunc etiam tecta erunt profana. Postea subjungit, [illegible, ~24 letters] [illegible, ~28 letters] , Si exstructa sint in profano spatio & aperta versus locum sanctum; interius ipsorum sanctum habetur, quoad esum oblationum sanctissimarum; attamen oblationes mediocres ibi manducare non licet: qui vero cum immunditie sua eo ingreditur, innocens habetur: tecta vero omnimode profana sunt. Hinc videmus, quì ob diversum portæ situm locus sanctitatem vel obtineat vel amittat: præterea quid de tectis etiam conclavium circa עזרה[?] extructorum censendum sit; ista nimirum sancta non haberi, ni pavimento loci sancti fuerint æqualia. Cæterum supremus Senatus, cujus in hoc conclavi sedes, duplex fuisse videtur pro rerum ecclesiasticarum & politicarum diversitate: quoniam Deut. 17. 12. ubi de supremis senatoribus agitur, manifeste Sacerdos à Judice distinguitur, [illegible, ~12 letters] ad Sacerdotem aut ad Judicem, i. Sacerdotes aut Judices; ut com. 9. indicio est, ubi pro Sacerdote ponuntur Sacerdotes. Adde, Je-hoschaphatum, cum judicia Hierosolymis restauraret, duos ordines constituisse, Sacerdotes & Capita familiarum, ad judicium Dei, & ad litem: similiter duos præsides commat. 11. unum [illegible, ~8 letters] ad omnem causam Dei; alterum, scil. ducem Judæorum, [illegible, ~8 letters] ad omne negotium regis. Quibus succinunt verba Ier. 19. 1. quibus Seniores populi à Senioribus

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek passages are mostly too small or faint at this resolution to read letter by letter; they are marked illegible with approximate letter counts, except the single words עזרה[?] and ἰσόπεδα[?], which are doubtful. The line "Sacer-" at the foot is a catchword and is kept out of the text. The text runs as one paragraph from the previous page; no indented paragraph start is visible. Long s has been rendered as plain s. No printing errors were clearly identified.
